prompt: Use your immediately prior diagnosis as context. Answer only this narrow engineering question, without re-inspecting the repository: design ONE unmistakable wet-branch-only diagnostic for the Web Audio headphone app. A simple L/R swap is rejected because centered music may hide it. The diagnostic must be impossible to miss on ordinary music, must temporarily bypass normal masterGain, and must distinguish whether the wet branch reaches the output at all. Prefer something like hard-muting one output ear or routing only one known wet channel to one ear. Give: (1) the exact minimal graph/gain-node arrangement, (2) exact button behavior, (3) what the listener should hear if the wet branch is working, (4) what it means if they do not hear that, and (5) whether your prior conclusion still stands that self-normalizing masterGain is the leading reason Spatial ON/OFF is too subtle. Keep the answer under 500 words. Do not propose tuning values or multiple fixes.
context: Your prior verified diagnosis said the dry/wet crossfade is correct, the self-normalizing masterGain likely cannibalizes cue increases, mono/near-mono source is second possibility, Safari routing bug third.
Whole-output 400 Hz DSP proof is audibly working, but that does not prove wetMerge/wetGain.
Need one decisive wet-only proof before any more DSP changes.
expected_response: Under 500 words. One wet-only proof, exact minimal implementation and binary interpretation, plus confirm/revise the prior masterGain diagnosis.
